title: She Quit Being An Idol, Then Everyone Who Hurt Her Image Started Dying . . .
caption:
In Perfect Blue, pop idol Mima Kirigoe quits her girl group to become an actress, and the people around her start turning up dead.
A stalker, a fake diary website and a ghost in the mirror close in. Follow for more anime recaps!

#perfectblue #anime #animerecap #animemovie #fyp
comment: Did you see Rumi as the killer coming, or did you suspect Me-Mania? Why?

segments.say: Her own manager puts on a red idol dress and chases her through the night with a *knife*.
To see how it got here, go back to the day pop idol Mima decides to *quit*.
Her group Cham is not selling, so the agency wants Mima to become an *actress*.
Rumi, her manager and a former idol herself, thinks Mima is making a huge *mistake*.
The agency boss waves her off, because pop idols do not make money any *more*.
But Mima has made up her mind, so she tells the fans at her last show that she is *leaving*.
A brawl breaks out in the crowd, and a creepy man with a bloody nose never takes his eyes off *her*.
She sings her final song as an idol, and the fans cry with *her*.
Her fans call her Mimarin, and one of them is not ready to let her *go*.
Afterward, one fan hands her flowers, and the creepy man watches from the *crowd*.
At home, she feeds her fish, and finds a pink envelope with a heart on *it*.
Then her mom calls. Mima says the singing is over, and she is going to be an *actress*.
That night, a fax slides out of her machine with one word on it. *Traitor*.
Still, she lands a small part in a murder drama called Double Bind. She has exactly one *line*.
Her one line is, excuse me, who are you? It sounds like a joke now, but it will not stay one.
Then a fan letter addressed to Mima explodes in the hands of her agency boss, *Tadokoro*.
Mima knows that letter was meant for her. She could have been the one who opened *it*.
Rumi tells her it was only a prank, and nobody calls the police.
Rumi sets up a computer for her, and Mima finds a fan site called Mima's *Room*.
It is her own diary, written in her own voice, and it knows what she bought at the *store*.
Rumi says it is just a website, and Mima tries to believe her.
Then the script for Double Bind arrives, and her character has to go through a brutal assault in a strip *club*.
Rumi says no way. Mima is a pop *idol*.
But Mima says she is an actress now, and she takes the *scene*.
That was her first big *mistake*.
She shoots the brutal scene, and when it is over, she barely feels like *herself*.
The more she changes, the angrier her fans get, and the magazines love every *minute*.
Then a new post appears on her site. Help me, everyone is forcing me to do it, and it blames the *screenwriter*.
At night, her old idol self smiles at her from the TV, and she cannot look *away*.
That night, her old idol self shows up and tells her she is *filthy*.
Mima begs the ghost to stop, but her idol self only *laughs*.
Soon after, the screenwriter is stalked in a parking garage, and the next day he is found *dead*.
The news says he was stabbed again and again, and Mima is scared the killer is punishing everyone who changed her *image*.
Mima agrees to a risky photo shoot, because she wants to prove she is no longer a pop *idol*.
But backstage, her idol self appears again and says this is what everyone really *wants*.
In a room full of her photos, a stalker called Me-Mania decides the new Mima is a fake, and swears to *protect* the real one.
Then the show's director is stabbed to death, too, and the news says the killer is still out *there*.
Mima finds a blood-stained bag in her room, and she cannot remember how it got *there*.
She starts to wonder if she is the one doing the *killing*.
In Double Bind, her character turns out to have a split personality, and the doctor says an illusion can never become *real*.
When the last scene of the drama wraps, everyone cheers, but Mima cannot tell where the show ends and her life *begins*.
Late that night, Me-Mania catches her alone and pins her down with a *knife*.
He says he is protecting the real Mima, and Mima is just an *imposter*.
Mima fights back, grabs the knife, and he drops to the *floor*.
She stumbles out, and Rumi pulls her into a *hug*.
Rumi drives her home and asks if she is sure it was not just a *dream*.
At Mima's apartment, Rumi says she needs to make a call and steps out of the *room*.
When Mima turns around, Rumi is standing there in a red idol dress, and she says this is her *room* now.
She talks about Rumi like a stranger and calls herself the one true *Mima*.
Then she grabs a knife, and Mima runs for her *life*.
They race through the dark streets, and Rumi in her red dress never *slows*.
Rumi catches her, and they fight tooth and nail on the *ground*.
Mima grabs something and hits her in the face. Blood runs down the *dress*.
Rumi staggers back onto the highway, and a truck hits her head *on*.
The real killer was Rumi, the manager who never got over her own idol *days*.
Months later, Mima visits a quiet hospital, where Rumi still thinks she is the real *idol*.
A nurse says that once in a while, Rumi slips back into her old *self*.
Mima thanks her anyway, and says goodbye for *good*.
On the drive home, Mima looks in the mirror and smiles. She finally knows who she *is*.
